prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
As of September 2026, a new wish is becoming clearer in Japan.

Many young travelers, especially men under 30, want trips that follow their own pace. In a 2025 survey, their top choices included solo travel, at about 25%, and trips to spend more time on a hobby, at about 24%.

Another survey asked a different question: If people could take one month off, how long would they want to travel? The most common answer was about one week, chosen by about 24% of respondents.

Together, these answers suggest a desire for slower and more personal travel.

But the picture changes when we look at actual trip plans.

In another survey of people planning an autumn trip, the average stay was 1.8 nights. The middle answer was two nights.

So the wish is longer than the usual trip.

A national tourism report also says that increasing the length of stays is still an important policy goal. This means the country has not yet fully moved from quick sightseeing to long, slow stays.

The interesting story is not that young people have already changed the way they travel. It is that their travel dreams seem to be changing before their travel behavior does.

【Point One】
Slow travel may first mean having control over your time. In an official survey, about 90% of Japanese Gen Z respondents wanted free time during an overseas tour. About 80% wanted at least half a day. They may still join a tour, but they want a large part of the trip to be their own. Travel businesses may respond with more free time and optional plans, even before people can take week-long holidays.

【Point Two】
Young people do not all want the same kind of trip. Men under 30 showed strong interest in solo travel and hobby-focused travel. Among women under 30, gourmet travel was popular at about 52%, and visiting famous places was still high at about 45%. So the trend is not a universal rejection of sightseeing. Travel destinations may need different choices for self-directed trips, food trips, and famous attractions.

point_one.reasoning: Gen Zの約90％が海外ツアー中の自由時間を望み、約80％が半日以上を望むという具体的な調査結果を追加している。これにより、長期休暇が難しくても、旅行者の主導権を高める商品設計が有効だという実務的な示唆が得られる。

point_two.reasoning: 女性 under 30ではグルメ旅行が約52％、有名地訪問が約45％という性別別の具体データを加え、若者全体が観光を拒否しているわけではないと明確にしている。旅行先や事業者が、自由行動・食・定番観光を一律に扱わず、異なる需要向けに選択肢を分けるべきだという示唆がある。
